newsitem.title: FRANCE: U.S. ambassador to Paris Harriman dead at 76.
newsitem.headline: U.S. ambassador to Paris Harriman dead at 76.

text.p: Pamela Harriman, the U.S. ambassador to France, died in Paris on Wednesday two days after she was taken ill with of a brain haemorrhage, the U.S. embassy said. She was 76.

"She was one of the most unusual and gifted people I ever met," President Bill Clinton declared on hearing the news. "She was an extaordinary U.S. ambassador ... earning the trust of the leaders (of France) and the admiration of the people."

Harriman, a close Clinton supporter, had fallen ill on Monday evening at the Ritz Hotel in Paris where she had gone for a swim. She was taken to hospital by ambulance and later pronounced in serious condition.

Clinton chose her as envoy to Paris in 1993 as a reward for raising millions of dollars for his first presidential campaign. After four years in the job, she had been widely expected to retire later this year.
Harriman, was born in Farnborough, England, and became a U.S. citizen after marrying her third husband, the late multimillionaire and diplomat Averell Harriman, in 1971.

She was just 19 when she married Randolph Churchill, son of British prime minister Winston Churchill, during World War Two. They divorced as the war ended but the marriage produced her only child. Her second marriage was to cinema magnate Leyland Hayward in 1960.

"It is with sadness that we announce the death of Ambassador Pamela Harriman," U.S. Charge d'Affaires Donald Bandler said in a statement. "The Ambassador died this afternoon at the American Hospital of Paris."
"She was an inspIring leader and we all remember her with love and respect," he said.
